_comment: REFERENCE MANIFEST, NOT AN API PAYLOAD. Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager has no documented REST, Graph, or PowerShell write API for assessment creation, control mapping, or improvement-action status/evidence updates as of this writing (docs/automation-surface.md has no routing-table row for Compliance Manager; see design.md Section 2 - identical grounding to scenarios/compliance-manager/assess-against-iso27001/, scenarios/compliance-manager/pci-dss-assessment/, and scenarios/compliance-manager/soc2-assessment/). No script in this scenario's deploy/ folder reads or applies this file - it is a structured, versioned source of truth for the person completing the portal wizard in README.md Section 5, so the deployed assessment can be diffed against intent during review instead of relying on institutional memory of what was clicked.
regulationTier: Premium template - counts against the tenant's purchased or A5/E5/G5 3-free-premium-template allotment. See README.md Section 3.
regulationVersionNote: Compliance Manager's regulation catalog lists 'HIPAA/HITECH' as a single premium template under the US Government category. It does NOT have a versioned sibling the way ISO/IEC 27001 (:2013 vs :2022) or PCI DSS (v3.2.1 vs v4.0) do, but it DOES have a separately-listed, easy-to-confuse-with-it template in the same catalog: 'HITRUST' (the HITRUST CSF - a separate, independently governed certifiable framework maintained by the HITRUST Alliance that harmonizes many standards INCLUDING HIPAA, but is not the same thing as a HIPAA/HITECH assessment and has its own separate certification path). Select 'HIPAA/HITECH', not 'HITRUST', when the goal is a HIPAA/HITECH-specific readiness view. See README.md Section 11.
assessmentNameNote: Assessment names must be unique tenant-wide (Microsoft Learn: compliance-manager-assessments). Cannot be changed after creation without deleting and recreating.

group.name: Security & Compliance Assessments
group.note: If scenarios/compliance-manager/assess-against-iso27001/, scenarios/compliance-manager/pci-dss-assessment/, and/or scenarios/compliance-manager/soc2-assessment/ are already deployed in this tenant using this same group name, ADD this HIPAA/HITECH assessment to that existing group rather than creating a new one. If this is the tenant's first Compliance Manager assessment, create a new group with this name so future assessments join it. See design.md Section 6 for exactly what group membership does and does not buy you - the benefit is narrower than 'shared credit for every control.'
group.groupingRule: Microsoft documents that a group can contain multiple assessments for the SAME product only if each one is for a DIFFERENT regulation (compliance-manager-assessments, 'Groups for assessments'). ISO/IEC 27001:2022 + PCI DSS v4.0 + SOC 2 + HIPAA/HITECH in one group is four different regulations against the same Microsoft 365 product - an explicitly supported combination, not an edge case.

servicesInScopeNote: Multicloud (AWS/GCP/Azure via Defender for Cloud) scoping is out of scope for this scenario, matching scenarios/compliance-manager/assess-against-iso27001/design.md Section 7, scenarios/compliance-manager/pci-dss-assessment/design.md Section 8, and scenarios/compliance-manager/soc2-assessment/design.md Section 8's identical non-goal, and this library's tenant-only scope (AGENTS.md Section 5).

roleAssignments.note: Identical Compliance Manager role model to every other assessment in this library - assign the narrowest role that does the job. See README.md Section 3. NOTE: HIPAA itself separately requires the covered entity/business associate to formally DESIGNATE a Privacy Officer (45 CFR Section 164.530(a)(1)) and a Security Officer (45 CFR Section 164.308(a)(2)) - these are HIPAA-mandated organizational roles, not Compliance Manager RBAC roles, and are not satisfied merely by assigning someone Compliance Manager Administration.

recommendedStarter.assignTo: The person creating and owning this assessment (1-2 people, not the whole security team) - ideally the organization's designated HIPAA Security Officer or a delegate

Control owners across IT/Security/Compliance/Privacy (HIPAA's Privacy Rule, Security Rule, and Breach Notification Rule span legal, clinical-operations, and technical stakeholders, not just IT) who will test and update improvement actions but should not create new assessments
Internal auditors, the organization's designated Privacy Officer/Security Officer if not already a Contributor, and leadership who need visibility without edit rights

recommendedDeploymentOrder: scenarios/information-protection/auto-label-confidential-sharepoint/ and .../auto-label-confidential-exchange/ (labeling/encrypting documents likely to contain ePHI at rest and in transit - Technical Safeguards Section 164.312(a)/(e))
scenarios/dlp/exchange-pii-exfil-block/ (+ Part 2) (blocking unauthorized transmission of ePHI-adjacent identifiers over email - Technical Safeguards Section 164.312(e), Transmission Security)

scenarios/dlp/endpoint-dlp-usb-block/ (+ Adaptive Protection variant) (controlling removable media that could carry ePHI off-network - Physical Safeguards Section 164.310(d), Device and Media Controls)

scenarios/adaptive-protection/block-legacy-authentication/ and .../exchange-legacy-auth-block/ (access control and person/entity authentication - Technical Safeguards Section 164.312(a)/(d); Administrative Safeguards Section 164.308(a)(4), Access Authorization)
scenarios/insider-risk/departing-employee-data-theft/ (workforce security and termination procedures - Administrative Safeguards Section 164.308(a)(3))
scenarios/audit/premium-audit-investigation/ (information system activity review and audit controls - Administrative Safeguards Section 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D); Technical Safeguards Section 164.312(b))
scenarios/audit/compromised-account-incident-response/ (incident response feeding the required breach risk assessment - Breach Notification Rule, 45 CFR Sections 164.400-414)
THEN create this assessment - built-in automation (design.md Section 4) picks up signals from controls already in place, reducing the manual-testing backlog a Contributor/Assessor faces on day one.

controlCrosswalk._comment: This is THIS LIBRARY'S OWN correlation of its scenarios to HIPAA/HITECH's own published rule structure (Privacy Rule, Security Rule's three safeguard categories, Breach Notification Rule - 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164) - it is NOT a reproduction of Microsoft's proprietary per-improvement-action automation mapping (which isn't published in a form this scenario can fetch and cite - see design.md Section 7, same constraint scenarios/compliance-manager/assess-against-iso27001/design.md Section 6, scenarios/compliance-manager/pci-dss-assessment/design.md Section 7, and scenarios/compliance-manager/soc2-assessment/design.md Section 7 document for their own regulations). Use it to decide deployment order and to brief the organization's designated Privacy/Security Officer on what this tenant's Microsoft 365 controls contribute - do not present it to HHS OCR (in the event of an investigation) or a business-partner auditor as Microsoft's own control mapping, and do not present it as proof the organization's own required Security Risk Analysis (45 CFR Section 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)) is complete (that analysis is the organization's own legal obligation - see README.md Section 2/Section 11).

categories.coverage: Out of scope for direct technical automation from this Microsoft 365/Purview-only library - minimum-necessary use/disclosure restrictions and patient right-of-access request handling are organizational/legal processes this library does not script. The closest existing technical building block is PHI identification itself: Microsoft Purview ships a built-in 'U.S. Health Insurance Act (HIPAA) Enhanced' DLP policy template (SSN + DEA Number + U.S. Physical Addresses + All Full Names sensitive information types AND ICD-9-CM/ICD-10-CM keyword terms AND the Healthcare/Health-Medical-Forms trainable classifiers) that this library has not yet wrapped in a dedicated scenario - see PROGRESS.md follow-up.

scenarios/insider-risk/departing-employee-data-theft/ (Section 164.308(a)(3) - workforce security/termination procedures), scenarios/audit/premium-audit-investigation/ (Section 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D) - information system activity review), scenarios/adaptive-protection/block-legacy-authentication/ and .../exchange-legacy-auth-block/ (Section 164.308(a)(4) - access authorization procedures).

Largely out of scope for this Microsoft 365/Purview-only library - facility access controls and workstation physical security are an Azure-datacenter/physical-office concern, not a Purview one. Partial coverage only: scenarios/dlp/endpoint-dlp-usb-block/ (+ the Defender for Endpoint device-control family) addresses Section 164.310(d), Device and Media Controls, for the subset of that standard concerned with removable electronic media leaving the network with ePHI on it - disposal, accountability, and media re-use of physical devices themselves are not addressed.

scenarios/adaptive-protection/block-legacy-authentication/, .../exchange-legacy-auth-block/ (Section 164.312(a)/(d) - access control, person/entity authentication), scenarios/audit/premium-audit-investigation/ (Section 164.312(b) - audit controls), scenarios/information-protection/auto-label-confidential-sharepoint/, .../auto-label-confidential-exchange/ (Section 164.312(a)/(e) - encryption supporting access control and transmission security), scenarios/dlp/exchange-pii-exfil-block/ (+ Part 2) (Section 164.312(e) - transmission security).

scenarios/audit/compromised-account-incident-response/ (post-compromise response feeding the required breach risk assessment), scenarios/audit/premium-audit-investigation/ (forensic investigation and log review supporting that risk assessment). This library does not script the notification obligations themselves (notifying affected individuals, HHS, and - for breaches affecting 500+ residents of a state or jurisdiction - the media), which are organizational/legal processes, not a Purview policy.

controlCrosswalk.addressableNotOptionalNote: For the three Security Rule safeguard categories (Administrative, Physical, Technical), HIPAA's own rule text distinguishes 'required' from 'addressable' implementation specifications - but 'addressable' does NOT mean optional. An organization must implement every addressable specification as written, OR document why it is not reasonable/appropriate and implement an equivalent alternative measure, OR document why no safeguard is needed. See README.md Section 11 - this is the single most common HIPAA Security Rule misunderstanding this scenario has found grounded documentation for, and the manifest-structural check in validate/Test-ComplianceManagerAuditTrail.ps1 confirms each Security Rule category still carries this flag rather than letting it be silently dropped in a future edit.

auditMonitoring.note: These 3 operations are TENANT-WIDE Compliance Manager events, not scoped to a single assessment. This scenario deliberately REUSES scenarios/compliance-manager/assess-against-iso27001/deploy/Export-ComplianceManagerAuditTrail.ps1 (also copied into scenarios/compliance-manager/pci-dss-assessment/deploy/ and scenarios/compliance-manager/soc2-assessment/deploy/) rather than shipping a fourth, functionally-identical copy - run ONE instance against a shared CSV path if more than one of these scenarios is deployed. See design.md Section 2 and README.md Section 5.

notAValidHipaaCertification: A Compliance Manager assessment - however complete - is an internal readiness-tracking and evidence tool. There is currently no certification standard that the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services approves to demonstrate HIPAA/HITECH compliance by a business associate (Microsoft's own published position, cited in README.md Section 2/Section 11) - this assessment does not create one, and must never be presented as 'HIPAA certified.' It also does not substitute for the organization's own legally required Security Risk Analysis (45 CFR Section 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)) or for a signed Business Associate Agreement between the organization and Microsoft (and any subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI). See README.md Section 2/Section 11.
